steps.before: 5.1 Conclusion. If in addition the immersion $i$ is a closed immersion, the same argument applies verbatim; the only simplification in that case is that the image is closed, so the shrinking step 1.3 may be replaced by choosing a chart $U_i$ containing $i(x)$, whose preimage $X\cap U_i$ is affine as a closed subscheme of the affine scheme $U_i$. ## Remarks

Write $\alpha_{n+1}\colon A_{n+1}\to A_n$, $\beta_{n+1}\colon B_{n+1}\to B_n$, and $\gamma_{n+1}\colon C_{n+1}\to C_n$ for the transition maps. The short exact sequence of inverse systems has exact rows and commuting squares:

```tikzcd
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=large, column sep=large, cells={nodes={font=\Large}}, every label/.append style={font=\large}]
0 \arrow[r] & A_{n+1} \arrow[r, "f_{n+1}"] \arrow[d, "\alpha_{n+1}"'] & B_{n+1} \arrow[r, "g_{n+1}"] \arrow[d, "\beta_{n+1}"'] & C_{n+1} \arrow[r] \arrow[d, "\gamma_{n+1}"] & 0 \\
0 \arrow[r] & A_n \arrow[r, "f_n"'] & B_n \arrow[r, "g_n"'] & C_n \arrow[r] & 0
\end{tikzcd}
```

In particular, the right square and $\gamma_{n+1}(c_{n+1})=c_n$ give $g_n(\beta_{n+1}(b))=c_n$ for $b\in E_{n+1}$, which is the restriction $E_{n+1}\to E_n$ used in step 1.2. The proof above is independent of this illustration.
